title: A strip across the bottom shows every moving part on one cycle
goal: When two parts of one drawing move, the question is how they sit against each other in time, and that cannot be read in a column of numbers. So the timing lives in a strip across the bottom of the window: one lap of the motion, a bar for every moving property, and you drag one bar against another to set the lag between them.
notes:
Slice 3 of 5 from the answered study, and the part the user asked for in their own words: the timing should be on a surface bigger than the property panel.

MOCK: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-phase-wt.html (Make the knob lag the bell), steps 3, 4 and 7. Step 4 is the test the mock set itself: dragging the knob 90 ms later is impossible in a column. Step 7 shows the knob still finishing when the bell restarts, which is what the dashed repeats line is for.

SHARED WIDGET: the study found this is the same component the video timeline uses (docs/design/mocks/shared/components/inspector.css defines .timeline, .ruler, .track > .tl + .lane, .playhead, and both the icon and video mocks build from it). Build it so video can take it later without a rewrite. What must NOT be shared is what the ruler measures: an icon strip is one cycle with no end, a video strip is a document with a last frame.

Start and Over on a bar are the same two numbers as the fields in the Motion entry. One model, two views.

Next release only.
acceptance: A strip across the bottom shows one cycle, measured in milliseconds, with a lane for each moving property grouped under the layer it belongs to
Dragging a bar sideways changes when that motion starts, dragging its ends changes how long it takes, and the numbers in the right hand panel follow at once
The gap between two bars is shown as a number while you drag one against the other
A dashed line marks where the cycle starts again, and a bar is allowed to carry on past it
The strip can be hidden and shown again, and a document with nothing moving does not show it at all

log.note: deps set: the motion model lands first, then this

Adversarial review BEFORE building, walking the mock (icon-phase-wt, steps 3/4/7) as a first-time user.

1. THE MOCK'S RULER CANNOT DO ITS OWN STEP 7. The landed model derives the cycle: motionCycleLengthMS is the LONGEST motion's end. So dragging the knob's bar to 90..990 makes the cycle 990 and the bar can never run past the repeats line, which is the exact thing step 7 is about, and acceptance item 4 demands. Worse, a derived cycle RESCALES THE RULER WHILE YOU DRAG: the bar chases the pointer and the drag is unusable. So the cycle becomes a real number on the document (motionCycleMS, optional, nil = follows the longest motion). Grabbing a bar pins it for the length of the drag; if the drag ends without overrunning, it goes back to automatic, so the pin is invisible unless it is doing something.

2. THE STRIP IS NOT THE PANEL'S LIST. The Motion list speaks for ONE picked layer. A lag is between TWO layers, so the strip reads the whole document, grouped by layer. Clicking a bar has to pick that layer so the panel follows, or you are looking at a bar you cannot edit.

3. WHICH GAP IS 'THE GAP'? The mock draws one bracket from 0 to the knob's start, which only reads as a lag because the bell happens to start at 0. With five bars that number means nothing. So the readout measures to the NEAREST OTHER BAR EDGE and names it: '90 ms after Bell body'. That is the relationship a person is actually making.

4. CUT: the mock's Fit button. With the span fixed at the cycle plus headroom it always fits, so Fit is a button that does nothing.

5. CUT FROM THIS SLICE: dragging the playhead to scrub. The mock argues against it (you cannot usefully scrub 900ms; you slow the loop instead) and it is a separate value from the lag. Left out, written into the audit's rough.

6. SWIFTUI CANNOT TAKE A SYNTHESIZED DRAG (docs/design/playtest-harness.md). So every number the drag decides goes into PhotonzCore as a pure tested type and the view is a thin shell, with a probe a walk drives, exactly the precedent InspectorSectionDragProbe set.

SHIPPED, with one honest hole: nothing was photographed and no walk ran.

WHAT LANDED. Next only, behind next-motion-strip (needs next-motion). A dock across the bottom of the WHOLE window, under both canvas and side column, there only while the document has something moving in it. A lane per moving property, grouped under the layer it belongs to as a labelled hairline rather than a bar of its own (a layer does not occupy time; its properties do). Drag a bar to move its start, drag either end to change its duration; while you drag, the gap to the nearest end of any other bar is a bracket with the number and that layer's name on it. Picking a bar picks its layer. A dashed repeats line marks where the lap starts over and a bar is allowed to run past it. Option Command T, View menu, dimmed with nothing moving.

THE MODEL. PhotonzCore/MotionStrip.swift, written test-first: MotionStripLane/Group/Edge, motionStrip() and motionStripEdges(excluding:) on the document, MotionStripRuler (one lap plus a third, ticks off the 1/2/5 ladder), MotionStripDrag (the three grabs, the clamps, the snapping) and MotionStripGap. 37 tests. PhotonzDocument gained motionCycleMS: Int?, nil meaning the lap follows the longest motion, written to disk only when set so every existing document is byte for byte what it was; motionCycleLengthMS now honours it.

THE ONE RULE WORTH READING, in MotionStripCycle.after(drag:automatic:current:): a bar dragged past the end of the lap HOLDS the lap where it was and overruns it; a bar dragged back inside hands the lap back to following the longest motion. Without the first half nothing could ever overrun the restart, because the lap would swallow it, and step 7 of the mock would be impossible. Without the second, one drag out and back leaves a held number nobody asked for.

REVIEW OF THE BUILT THING (read, not run, because the screen was locked). Three real defects found and fixed: the lane width subtracted the strip's inset twice so every bar sat two dozen points short of the ruler above it; the lane label's indent sat outside its fixed width so every lane started ten points right of the dashed line; and the gap bracket was drawn eleven points above the top lane, where the scrolling area clipped it away. One design change on the same pass: the preview no longer PAUSES while a bar is dragged. displayDocument is handed the timing under the hand (the same bargain the pivot crosshair strikes), so the lag plays as you make it, which is the only way to judge whether ninety milliseconds is the right ninety.

VERIFIED: 37 core tests for the strip, full suite 6783 tests green, plain and playtest builds green.
NOT VERIFIED: anything on screen. The Mac's screen has been locked the whole task (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked true, checked twice), so macOS never draws the app and every walk refuses to run. Scripts/playtest/motion-timing-strip-walk.json is written and has never executed once. A whole-set sweep is requested for exactly this: the editor's body is now wrapped in a VStack so a dock can sit under it, which every walk's window goes through.

FOLLOW-UPS: filed escape-calls-off-a-drag-everywhere-it-can-be-sta (Escape cannot call off a bar drag; cancelMotionTimingDrag exists, nothing listens for the key, and the pivot drag may have the same hole). Folded into watch-a-motion-loop-at-the-sizes-it-will-really that the loop-speed control has to reach the strip's playhead, since a 90ms lag is under six frames and the strip now lets you set lags nobody can judge at full speed.

LEFT ROUGH, no task earned (each is in the audit so the user can react):
- No playhead scrubbing. The mock argues against it and it is a different value from the lag; it also wants the speed control that is not built.
- Cut the mock's Fit button: with the ruler always one lap plus a third it always fits, so Fit does nothing.
- Changed from the mock: the lag bracket measures to the nearest end of ANY other bar and names it, rather than running from the left edge of the strip, which only read as a lag in the mock's own two-bar example.
- Six or more moving properties makes the strip scroll rather than grow, and that has not been looked at on a short window.
